story.title: Don Toliver's London Concert Rescheduled Following Manchester Evacuation Incident
story.summary: Don Toliver's concert at the O2 in London has been rescheduled after an incident at his Manchester concert, where over 12,000 fans were evacuated due to the release of an unknown substance. More than 80 individuals received medical treatment, with one person hospitalized following the event at Co-op Live arena.

explore_lenses.label: Who is affected, and what support is available?
explore_lenses.title: Manchester attendees faced respiratory and eye symptoms
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate health impact was on people at the Manchester concert, while London ticket holders face a rescheduled show and automatic refunds. Authorities advised anyone who becomes ill after leaving the venue to seek hospital care.

claims.text: Greater Manchester Police said more than 12,000 attendees were safely escorted from Co-op Live and that one person had been taken to hospital.

The Associated Press reported that 89 people showed symptoms believed linked to the exposure; police cited eye and respiratory irritation among some concertgoers, and the remainder received dry decontamination at the scene.
Police advised people who attended and later notice side effects or become unwell to attend their local hospital.
The O2 says tickets for the postponed London date remain valid for December 15, 2026, and that refunds for the original London show will be processed automatically.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Public reporting does not establish the hospitalized person's condition or whether further attendees sought treatment after leaving.

explore_lenses.label: What does the evidence establish so far?
explore_lenses.title: The evacuation and emergency response are confirmed
explore_lenses.summary: Official police information and subsequent reporting establish a large-scale precautionary evacuation after concertgoers reported effects from a substance. The cause has not been determined.

claims.text: Venue staff alerted Greater Manchester Police shortly after 10 p.m. on November 22, 2026; emergency services then responded and began evacuating people when safe to do so.
Police declared a major incident, a coordination measure for emergency services and partner agencies, during the response.
Early reports described the material as believed to be tear gas, but police later characterized it as an unknown substance; that later description is the supported current characterization.
The O2 attributed the London postponement to production delays following the Manchester show, while Don Toliver said he wanted to ensure people were safe before the next performance proceeded.

explore_lenses.label: What remains unknown about the substance?
explore_lenses.title: Identification, origin and criminality remain open
explore_lenses.summary: Investigators had not publicly identified the substance as of November 24, 2026. That means reported symptoms and the initial tear-gas assessment should not be treated as a final forensic finding.

claims.text: Greater Manchester Police said enquiries were underway to determine both what the substance was and what caused the incident.
A senior police officer said investigators were seeking to establish the substance's nature, its origin and any associated risk, including whether criminality occurred.
Co-op Live said it was working with police to identify the cause, rather than claiming that the venue had established one.

story_report.summary: Don Toliver’s London concert at the O2 has been postponed after an unknown substance was released during his Manchester performance at Co-op Live, prompting the evacuation of more than 12,000 people. Emergency services treated dozens of attendees, and one person was taken to hospital. The London date has been rescheduled for Dec. 15, 2026, with existing tickets remaining valid and refunds for the original date to be issued automatically.

sections.heading: Manchester Emergency Response
sections.body: Venue staff alerted Greater Manchester Police shortly after 10 p.m. on Nov. 22, and emergency services began evacuating attendees when it was safe to do so. Police declared a major incident to coordinate the response with partner agencies. Greater Manchester Police said all attendees were safely escorted from the venue.

sections.heading: Attendees Receive Medical Treatment
sections.body: The Associated Press reported that 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be connected to the exposure. Some concertgoers reported eye and respiratory irritation, while the remaining affected people received dry decontamination at the scene. Police advised attendees who later experience side effects or become unwell to go to their local hospital.

sections.heading: Police Continue Substance Investigation
sections.body: Early reports described the material as believed to be tear gas, but police later said it was an unknown substance. Investigators are examining what the substance was, how the incident occurred, its origin and any potential associated risk, including whether criminality was involved. Co-op Live said it was working with police to identify the cause.

unresolved.text: Authorities have not publicly identified the substance, established how it entered the venue, attributed responsibility or announced an arrest or conclusion on criminal intent.
Public reporting does not establish the hospitalized person’s condition or whether additional attendees sought treatment after leaving the venue.

This marks Shah's first international trip since taking office in March. The visit also resulted in agreements on infrastructure projects, including a railway and a hydropower plant.

related_stories.title: Trump Claims Role in Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia Amid National Security Concerns
related_stories.summary: President Trump has claimed credit for the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, stating he communicated with the company's board to address concerns regarding national security. He emphasized that the government does not view Huang's return as a risk to national security and described the announcement as vital for Nvidia's success and the economy.

related_stories.title: U.S. Places Megaspeed on Trade Blacklist Amid Nvidia Scandal
related_stories.summary: The U.S. government has added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist, citing the firm's alleged connections to espionage and its role in the Nvidia scandal. This decision follows scrutiny over the company's ties to China and its controlling shareholder, Alice Huang, who has been implicated in an espionage investigation. The announcement coincided with the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia.

related_stories.title: South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Amid AI Cheating Controversy
related_stories.summary: Choi Kyo-jin, South Korea's education minister, has stepped down following backlash over last-minute security measures aimed at preventing AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam. The measures, which included the use of hidden cameras and smart glasses, sparked significant criticism and chaos during the exam process.
